stances.claim: Though the Duterte administration laudably chose diplomacy as the banner SCS strategy, the geopolitical reality is that 'the best way to assure peace is to be prepared for war' -- and the Philippines alone cannot match China's military might, having historically depended on US military assistance.
stances.rhetorical_move: diplomacy-plus-deterrence framing (diplomatic banner does not replace military preparedness)

stances.claim: PH dependence on US military assistance has paradoxically 'lulled us into complacency' -- even 25 years after the 1991 ouster of US bases, we still have not developed a strong military apparatus suited to our archipelagic territorial configuration; the Edca (2014) supplementing MDT (1951) and VFA (1999) reflects this continued dependency rather than independent capability.
stances.rhetorical_move: paradox-of-dependency framing (alliance enabling rather than displacing complacency)

stances.claim: The Saguisag v Ochoa (Jan 12, 2016) opinions present the foundational doctrinal split: Justice Carpio (concurring) defends the US alliance and Edca as 'absolutely necessary and essential' for prepositioning war materials, arguing that 'only one power on earth can deter militarily China' -- the US -- making the MDT 'utterly crucial' for EEZ defense; Justice Leonen (dissenting) counters that MDT/VFA were in effect when China invaded PH EEZ features and 'the Americans did not come to our aid,' with US commitment 'ambiguous' and the US 'will not interfere' in PH-China disputes.
stances.rhetorical_move: paired-opinion presentation (Carpio concurrence vs Leonen dissent without CJ endorsement)

stances.claim: National interest is the ultimate motivation of every country -- the PH filed arbitration to protect its EEZ, not to enhance US interests or harm China's claims; the US wants SCS navigation freedom for Obama's 'pivot to Asia' and will continue aggressive sail-and-flyover regardless of China, but whether the US will act decisively to enforce the decision's PH-favorable nitty-gritty will depend on US national/regional/international interests, US-China trade/political/financial relations, and consultation with European and Asian allies plus Russia-balancing.
stances.rhetorical_move: interest-realism framing (national interest as universal driver, US assistance contingent on broader calculations)

stances.claim: Additionally, US internal issues -- budget constraints, intensifying public revulsion of overseas interference, and especially the November 2016 election (Clinton continuity vs Trump radical change) -- make US-policy sustainability uncertain; bottom line: 'premature overdependence on US policy at this point may not be advisable.'
stances.rhetorical_move: uncertainty-cumulation closing (multiple US-domestic factors + election uncertainty → caution)

notable_anecdotes: The geopolitical axiom anchor: 'the best way to assure peace is to be prepared for war' -- used to frame the column's central tension between Duterte's diplomatic strategy and military-preparedness reality.

The 25-year complacency arc: 'Even after the ouster of the US bases in 1991, we have not developed a strong military apparatus that complements our archipelagic territorial configuration' -- using a quarter-century timeline to physicalize institutional drift.

Carpio's extensive concurring quote on Edca: 'In modern warfare, the prepositioning of war materials ... is absolutely necessary and essential to a successful defense against armed aggression, particularly for a coastal state like the Philippines... Such prepositioning will also publicly telegraph to the enemy that any armed aggression would be repelled.' The most extensively preserved Carpio quotation in any of CJ's SCS-related columns.

Carpio's 'only one power on earth' claim regarding US deterrence of China -- the most categorical strategic-dependency assertion in the column, deployed to frame the strongest case for the US alliance.

Leonen's matching dissent quotation on US non-aid: 'The 1951 Mutual Defense Treaty and the Visiting Forces Agreement [were] in effect when the Chinese invaded certain features within our Exclusive Economic Zone in the West Philippine Sea. The Americans did not come to our aid.' -- the operative refutation of Carpio's prepositioning argument, drawn from real historical experience.

The Obama-Clinton-Trump succession framing as outcome-determinant: Clinton = pivot continuation; Trump = 'a radical new direction may ensue' -- the column's only explicit US-electoral acknowledgment, prophetic given that A328 (Nov 20, 2016) would announce Trump's victory two months later.
The 'Middle Kingdom' epithet for China -- using the historical-Chinese self-designation as an unobtrusive editorial signal of historical-civilizational weight beyond Cold War framing.
The closing 'Bottom line' formulation -- CJ's signature column-ending convention for precision-summary verdicts.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban continues last Sunday's question of whether longstanding PH-US defense relations help or hinder enforcement of the July 2016 SCS arbitration victory. The Duterte administration has laudably chosen diplomacy as its banner SCS strategy, but the geopolitical reality is that 'the best way to assure peace is to be prepared for war' -- and the Philippines alone cannot match China's military might, having historically depended on US assistance. Paradoxically, that dependency has 'lulled us into complacency': even 25 years after the 1991 ouster of US bases, the PH has not developed a strong military apparatus suited to its archipelagic configuration. The 2014 Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (Edca) was meant to bolster the 1951 Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) and 1999 Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA), allowing US construction of new facilities and prepositioning of defense equipment, supplies, and materiel. The foundational doctrinal split appears in Saguisag v Ochoa (Jan 12, 2016): Justice Antonio T. Carpio's concurring opinion defends the alliance -- 'In modern warfare, the prepositioning of war materials is absolutely necessary and essential to a successful defense against armed aggression, particularly for a coastal state like the Philippines,' arguing that the PH cannot acquire anti-ship/anti-aircraft missiles off the shelf, that anti-ship missile operation requires airborne radar or satellite guidance, that China's air and naval bases will be completed by end-2016, and that 'only one power on earth ... can deter militarily China,' making the MDT 'utterly crucial.' Justice Marvic M.V.F. Leonen's dissent counters that the MDT/VFA were in effect when China invaded features within the PH EEZ and 'the Americans did not come to our aid,' that no 'clear, unequivocal, and binding commitment' was given on MDT applicability to PH WPS claims, that 'the commitment of the United States remains ambiguous,' and that the US 'will not interfere in those types of differences we have with China.' CJ's own answer: national interest is the ultimate motivation of every country on earth -- the PH filed and won arbitration to protect its EEZ, not to enhance American interests or harm China's claims. The US wants SCS navigation freedom for Obama's 'pivot to Asia' and will continue aggressive sail-and-flyover regardless of China; but whether the US will act as decisively to enforce the decision's PH-favorable nitty-gritty depends on US national, regional, and international interests, US-China trade/political/financial relations, and consultation with European and Asian allies plus Russia-balancing. The PH is not America's only friend. US internal issues (budget constraints, intensifying public revulsion of overseas interference) and the November 2016 election (Clinton continuity vs unpredictable Trump's potential radical new direction) make US-policy sustainability uncertain. Bottom line: 'Any premature overdependence on US policy at this point may not be advisable.'
